findings.message: REPORT_TOTALS sums only the rows that have a number, so a partial sum is shown as the full total. This applies to `cost_usd`, `agent_s`, `review_rounds` and `commits` (`[$rows[].x | numbers] | add`). A row whose value could not be read is either dropped from the sum or contributes 0, and the totals line, pane and HTML give no sign of it. A row with `agent_commits` missing because `git rev-list` failed, or `cost_usd` missing because the agent log has no result object (watchdog kill, truncated log), looks the same as a row that contributed nothing. Fix: count the rows that lack each summed field among the live or finished runs, for example `cost_unknown`. Show the total as partial (`$2.50 + ?` or `≥ $2.50`), or as `-` when any contributing row is unknown, in the bash table, view.ts and report.html.
findings.scenario: Two claude rows: 002-a has cost_usd=2.5 and agent_commits=7. 003-b was killed by the watchdog, so agent.log has no result line and its cost_usd is null; its rev-list also failed, so agent_commits is null. Then `report --json` gives totals.cost_usd == 2.5 and totals.commits == 7, and the pane prints `cost $2.50` and `7 commits` with no unknown marker, presenting one run's cost as the build's cost.

findings.message: The same report logic is written several times. The live-state set (`dispatched`, `running`) appears in REPORT_ROW (report-query.sh:13), REPORT_TOTALS (report-render.sh:5 and :10), report.sh:57, view.ts:3 and report.html:33. Duration formatting (`dur`) is in report-render.sh:14, view.ts:7 and report.html:25. Cost formatting and timeline spans are each in view.ts and report.html. view.ts recounts `running` from rows instead of using `totals.running`. A future state such as `queued` added in one place would make the band, the pane and the totals disagree. Use `totals.running` in view.ts and keep one state list per language.

`parseReport` accepts a version-1 snapshot whose `totals` object is missing fields or holds non-numbers, and silently sets `jobs`, `prs_open`, `unknown`, `running` and the others to 0. A malformed snapshot then shows a confident `0 PRs open`, with the unknown count hidden, instead of `report unreadable`. Treat a missing or non-numeric required total as unreadable. Only `wall_s` and `cost_usd` are legitimately null.

When the cluster reports the Job is gone (`$j.job == "-"`), the row's `job` becomes `-` instead of the job name in the record. The row loses the job name that the record had. Fall back to `$r.job` for `-` as well as `?`.

The README says the mod 'refreshes after any `specclaw-fleet trigger`, `status` or `report` Bash call'. The refresh only re-reads `.specclaw/fleet/report.json`, and only `report --save` writes that file, so after `trigger` or `status` the pane, band and status line show the same stale snapshot. Either say the views update only after `report --save`, or narrow FLEET_CALL to `report`.

The AbovePrompt band always appends one more row below the engine's output and ignores `e.props.maxRows`. When `next(e)` already fills `maxRows`, the band overflows or is clipped. Skip the band, or return only `below`, when the existing content uses all of `maxRows`.
